summary: Intermittent inference pauses experienced by customer due to SDK connection pool/backoff mis-tuning
description:
Issue summary: NimbusHealth reported intermittent 'inference pauses' where a subset of prediction requests observe 10–30s additional latency or time out. Impact: customer production traffic (dedicated capacity) experiences increased tail latency and occasional 504s; affects user-facing flows for triage generation.

Initial report: 2026-03-05 09:40 UTC — customer support ticket with sample request IDs and approximate timestamps attached. Customer reports issue spiky and correlated with traffic bursts and SDK retries.

Why this looks like SDK misconfiguration: error patterns and client-side telemetry show dense retry bursts with short initial backoff and exhausted HTTP/1.1 connection slots per process, leading to queued requests on the client and perceived server slowness. Server-side serving runtime did not show corresponding GPU saturation during the window; autoscaler shows short spikes but sustained capacity available.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NimbusHealth SDK v1.8.1 with default pool config (maxSockets=8, per-host limit) and aggressive retry (maxRetries=6, initialDelay=100ms, jitter disabled).
2) Replay customer traffic pattern: 50 requests/sec bursts for 30s then idle for 30s for 10 minutes (mix of streaming and non-streaming endpoints).
3) Observe client-side queueing in SDK: connection acquire times spike and request latency climbs despite healthy server metrics.
4) Simulate corrected config: increase maxSockets, enable exponential backoff with jitter, and reduce maxRetries — tail latency disappears in client traces.
logs: 2026-03-05T09:42:13Z ERROR sdk-js RetryHandler - request id=r-1357 attempt=4 delay=100ms status=429
2026-03-05T09:42:14Z INFO serving-runtime RequestQueue - backend queued 12 requests for 850ms
2026-03-05T09:42:14Z INFO autoscaler ScaleUp - added 2 nodes (scale reason: latency-spike)
investigation_notes: 03/05 10:00 UTC: Collected customer SDK logs and netstat output; observed per-process connection saturation and frequent short backoff windows (100ms fixed).
03/05 11:20 UTC: Correlated request timestamps with host-level connection counts — client-side queue latency aligns with perceived pauses; server GPUs not saturated (avg GPU util 35–55%).
03/05 13:05 UTC: Replayed traffic in staging with customer's SDK v1.8.1 default settings and reproduced tail latency; toggling backoff to exponential + jitter eliminated majority of long-tail events.

Hypothesis: aggressive optimistic retry and low connection headroom cause synchronized retry storms and TCP port/socket exhaustion on customer hosts; this creates queuing on the client which looks like server-side pauses to end users.

Cross-check: network metrics show increased ephemeral port churn on customer hosts during incidents; observed many ESTABLISHED->TIME_WAIT transitions consistent with many short-lived connections under load.
workaround: Customer temporary mitigation applied: raised SDK maxSockets to 32, reduced maxRetries to 2, enabled exponential backoff with jitter. Result: immediate reduction in observed tail latency and 504 errors. Customer applied config change to production at 2026-03-05 15:12 UTC.
proposed_fix: 1) Ship SDK patch (v1.8.2) with safer default: exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter, sensible maxRetries=3, and connection pool recommendations per-host. 2) Add SDK health-check guidance in Console and an alert when client-side acquire wait > 500ms. 3) Update dedicated onboarding docs to highlight pool sizing for high-burst traffic patterns.
resolution: Partial: customer applied workaround config and saw improvement. Pending SDK release and Console alert changes. Final resolution will be updated after SDK release (target: 2026-03-12).
follow_up_tasks: SDK: publish v1.8.2 with new backoff defaults and pool docs (owner: SDK team)
Console: add client-side telemetry ingestion + rule to surface acquire-wait anomalies (owner: Observability)
Support: reach out to top 15 dedicated customers with recommended pool/backoff config docs
